181506f8cb.q: What is the tea bag bill of materials problem that caused production delays?
181506f8cb.a: A company's Bill of Materials was incorrect because flags (Fähnchen) were listed under a service surcharge instead of as individual line items. When the company only had 600 flags in stock but needed to produce 1000 units, the production order would fail because the system didn't recognize the flag shortage until after the order was placed, causing constant production delays and back-and-forth communication.

4f0c2bb749.q: What are the main reasons why inefficient processes remain hidden in business operations?
4f0c2bb749.a: Processes remain unknown because employees solve immediate problems quickly without documenting why, creating temporary workarounds that become permanent practices over years. Since nobody is paid to question or optimize processes, and management only focuses on urgent fires rather than systemic improvements, the actual costs are never broken down by process—they just appear as a massive personnel expense with no visibility into what work is actually being done.

fc9b3ab0e3.q: How did the product sample fulfillment process create a 25-day inventory gap?
fc9b3ab0e3.a: When free product samples were ordered without a paid product, they went to customer care for packing and mailing. This depleted stock (500 units) that warehouse inventory systems didn't track as allocated. When new orders came in and stock showed only 50 pieces instead of 500, the company had to reorder, creating a 31-day lead time gap until the new shipment arrived—during which the product could not be sold.
